decisions.reason: The listed deliberate changes were meant as mutations to check the tests, but the wording read as behaviour. Reworded step 3 to say they make the forbidden behaviour on purpose and that the table is the behaviour.

Named every reason value from the errors page and gave each its duration, with a fixture for each row. Kept one departure from the suggestion: a 429 that is a valid object with no reason is a refill-only refusal, because the page says such answers come under load and are to be retried; made-up reasons and malformed bodies fail closed to the day.

Fetched the authentication and errors pages again, recorded their addresses, the date and the hash of the bytes, and tied the reason table to a text search of them. Stated that no real API answer exists yet and that the owner trial records one. This also showed the earlier cause of the 429 is not proven, which the plan now says.

Agreed: the project asks the owner before a security review and runs it only on request. Reworded the key increment to name the exposure, ask, and record either the review or the owner decision, and made the same fix in the other web-search plan.
